DILG Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA corner Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City http: //www.dilg.com.ph JAN 31 2020 OPINION NO. MAYOR EUGENIANO E. IBARRA Clarin, Bohol Dear Mayor Ibarra This has reference to your letter dated 05 August 2019 requesting for this Department's legal opinion on whether or not the Vice Mayor is allowed to chair a particular standing committee like the committee on appropriations, ways and means and personnel matters. Please be informed that the issue at hand has long been settled by the Department in DILG Legal Opinion No. 76, series of 2007. Quoted hereunder are relevant portion of said legal opinion: "In reply thereto, please be informed that your query can be answered from the provisions of your adopted Internal Rules of Procedure (IRP). Allow us then to show you how we came up with such conclusion. The sources of Parliamentary Rules of Procedure of a Sanggunian, as a legislative or deliberative body, are arranged in the order of hierarchy, to wit: (1) the 1987 Constitution; (2) the Local Government Code; (3) Judicial Decisions; (4) Adopted Internal Rules of Procedure of the Sanggunian; (5) Parliamentary Practice; (6) Parliamentary Authors; and (7) Customs and Usage. When we say "arranged in the order of hierarchy", we mean that the higher source Shal/ take precedence over the lower source. In other words, the lower source can only be applied in the absence of the higher source. xxx xxx xxx Consequently, the IRP of the Sanggunian can only provide for matters that are not yet governed by the Local Government Code source, particularly sections 48 to 59 of the Local Government Code and other applicable laws. Hence, since as earlier stated, Sections 49 and 50 are silent as to whether or not the Vice Governor as Presiding Officer can hold or chair a regular committee, this matter can be properly dealt with in the Adopted IRP of the Sanggunian. Therefore, if the adopted IRP expressly prohibits the Vice Governor as Presiding Officer to hold a regular committee, then said provision of the IRP shall prevail. However, if the adopted IRP is silent on the matter, then we have to go down to the next lower source, which is "Parliamentary Practice". Under settled Parliamentary Practice, a Presiding Officer is not allowed

to hold or chair a regular but may be allowed to hold or chair a special or Ad Hoc committee for special purpose. " Applying the foregoing, your query, therefore, can be answered by the applicable provisions of the Adopted IRP of your Sanggunian. We hope we have enlightened you on the matter. Ve truly ours, Se Cc: RD Leocadio T. Trovela DILG Region VII Sudlon, Lahug Cebu City LLLS/I/ M. ANO ary DILG.OSEC
